a.how.1: Every night the site collects remote jobs from public job boards and employers' own career pages, reads each ad to work out who can apply from where, and keeps only jobs posted in the last 60 days.
a.how.2: When you add your CV, your browser splits it into short passages, leaves out your contact details, and turns each passage into a list of numbers that captures its meaning. It does the same comparison against every job and ranks them by the closest passage.
a.how.3: “Who can apply” comes from the ad's own words first (“must reside in”, “authorized to work in”, “solo residentes en”), then the location the board gives. When the ad names nothing, the job is marked “location not stated” and hidden by default.
a.how.4: Quick match skips the model download and ranks jobs by the words they share with your CV. It is faster on phones and less accurate.
a.privacy.1: Your CV never leaves your browser. There are no accounts, no server, no database, no analytics and no cookies. The site remembers your language and theme in this browser only.
a.privacy.2: You can check this yourself: open your browser's developer tools, go to the Network tab and run a match. The only requests are downloads of the job list and the matching model.
a.privacy.3: The one exception is the optional fit notes, which you switch on with your own AI key. Those send your CV to the provider you pick.
